errorCodes.meaning: `did` is not a network whose entry here is `acknowledged` and names the URL it is reached at — it is absent, a community, not (or no longer) a member, or names no URL.

The member network's signed index could not be fetched, answered for another network, did not verify, or could not be read. Its graph is indeterminate, not empty (VTI-REG-012). `details.reason` says which.

Credential.description: A DTG credential (W3C VC 2.0, JSON) exactly as signed. Verified by the party relying on it, never by its shape here: it is an open object so a binding cannot narrow away a member the proof covers.

Edge.description: One credential, from issuer to subject. A membership is two edges: the grant and the acknowledgement.

EdgeStatus.description: The credential's status as far as this network can determine it. `unchecked` is a credential whose status list this network does not hold.

EntryState.description: `listed`: the network lists the party and the party has not answered; this is never membership (VTI-VTN-013). `acknowledged`: the party acknowledged the network's grant; it is a member. `repudiated`: the party rejected the listing. `suspended`: the network suspended the membership; reversible. `removed`: the network ended the entry. `departed`: the party left, by repudiating the grant.

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

Membership.description: A person's membership credential (VMC) from a community that is a member of this network, holder-bound to the requester's identity. Open for the same reason as `Credential`.

root.description: Whether this is the network whose graph it is.

state.description: Its entry's state; absent for the root.

url.description: Where a member network is reached, so a viewer can expand it.

Response.description: The member network's graph, from its verified signed index.
Response.title: VTN Graph — Member Network — response payload
